cleared_risks.description: The overflow is not introduced by this change: the old code also summed with `samples.iter().sum::<u32>()` (e4), so the u32 accumulator is unchanged (e1). The real regression is separate: removing the `is_empty` early return (e4) means `average(&[])` now computes `0 / 0` as u32 and panics with divide-by-zero in both debug and release (e1), and `report(&[])` calls it, so this is a P1 defect a reviewer should raise under a different hypothesis.
cleared_risks.name: u32 sum can overflow for large samples

findings.body:
The change removed the `samples.is_empty()` guard in `average` (src/lib.rs lines 3-4 now compute `total / samples.len() as u32` directly). For an empty slice, both total and len are 0, so the integer division panics with divide-by-zero instead of returning 0 as the doc comment on line 1 promises. The only in-file caller, `report` (line 8), passes its samples straight through with no guard, so `report(&[])` now panics where it previously returned "mean=0".

Trigger: Calling report(&[]) or average(&[]), e.g. with a window that contains no samples.

Impact: Any caller of `fixture::report` (or `fixture::average`) with an empty sample set now panics. Callers that relied on the documented 0 result for empty input will crash or abort, and the doc comment no longer matches behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Restore the empty-slice guard: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
findings.title: average panics with divide-by-zero on empty input, breaking report() and the documented contract

findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed. For an empty slice, samples.iter().sum() is 0 and samples.len() as u32 is 0, so the integer division total / 0 runs. Unsigned integer division by zero panics in Rust in both debug and release builds. The doc comment on line 1 still promises 0 for no samples, so the function now contradicts its own contract.

Trigger: Calling average with an empty slice, directly or through report().”,

Impact: Any caller of the public average(&[]) panics. The in-file caller report() (line 8) passes its slice straight through, so report(&[]) also panics and would crash a caller that formats a report for an empty sample set. I did not confirm that any real caller passes an empty slice, so reachability depends on those callers.
findings.suggestion: Restore the guard: if samples.is_empty() { return 0; } before the division.
findings.title: average divides by zero on empty input

findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed, so `average` now computes `total / samples.len() as u32` with `samples.len() == 0`. Integer division by zero panics. The doc comment on line 1 still promises "or 0 when there are none", so the code now contradicts its own contract. `report` at line 8 calls `average(samples)` with no guard, so `report(&[])` panics too.

Trigger: Calling average(&[]) or report(&[]), for example when a sample set has no entries.

Impact: Any caller that passes an empty slice to `average` or `report` now panics instead of getting 0. This breaks the documented public contract. The only resolved caller I found is `report` in the same file, and it does not check for empty input. I did not find an external caller outside the file, and the caller search was partial (4 omitted), so the hypothesis's external-caller claim is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Restore the `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` guard before the division, or update the doc comment and the callers to handle the empty case explicitly.
findings.title: average() panics on empty slice (divide by zero) despite documented 0 return

risk_level.reason: The empty-slice guard in average was removed, so an empty input now divides by zero and panics, and the change touches a public function with a caller elsewhere, while the config tries to ignore src/** for review.
